agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

use builtin;
use str;

set edit:completion:arg-completer[melody] = {|@words|
    fn spaces {|n|
        builtin:repeat $n ' ' | str:join ''
    }
    fn cand {|text desc|
        edit:complex-candidate $text &display=$text' '(spaces (- 14 (wcswidth $text)))$desc
    }
    var command = 'melody'
    for word $words[1..-1] {
        if (str:has-prefix $word '-') {
            break
        }
        set command = $command';'$word
    }
    var completions = [
        &'melody'= {
            cand -o 'Write to a file'
            cand --output 'Write to a file'
            cand --generate-completions 'Outputs completions for the selected shell To use, write the output to the appropriate location for your shell'

            cand -h 'Print help'

        }
    ]
    $completions[$command]

using namespace System.Management.Automation
using namespace System.Management.Automation.Language

Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'melody' -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)

    $commandElements = $commandAst.CommandElements
    $command = @(
        'melody'
        for ($i = 1; $i -lt $commandElements.Count; $i++) {
            $element = $commandElements[$i]
            if ($element -isnot [StringConstantExpressionAst] -or
                $element.StringConstantType -ne [StringConstantType]::BareWord -or
                $element.Value.StartsWith('-') -or
                $element.Value -eq $wordToComplete) {
                break
        }
        $element.Value
    }) -join ';'

    $completions = @(switch ($command) {
        'melody' {
            [CompletionResult]::new('-o', '-o', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Write to a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--output', '--output', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Write to a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--generate-completions', '--generate-completions', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Outputs completions for the selected shell To use, write the output to the appropriate location for your shell')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-t', '-t', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against a string')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--test', '--test', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against a string')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-f', '-f', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--test-file', '--test-file', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Test the compiled regex against the contents of a file')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-n', '-n', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print output with no color')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--no-color', '--no-color', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print output with no color')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-r', '-r', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Start the Melody REPL')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--repl', '--repl', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Start the Melody REPL')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-h', '-h', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print help')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--help', '--help', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print help')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-V', '-V ', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print version')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--version', '--version', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print version')
            break
        }
    })

    $completions.Where{ $_.CompletionText -like "$wordToComplete*" } |
        Sort-Object -Property ListItemText
}

import os, pty, sys, select, time
# usage: ptyi.py <delay> cmd args... ; reads stdin as script: lines to send (each with \n), separated by time delay
def run(argv, lines, delay=0.3, timeout=5.0):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.execvp(argv[0], argv)
    out = b''
    def drain(t):
        nonlocal out
        end = time.time() + t
        while time.time() < end:
            r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.05)
            if r:
                try:
                    data = os.read(fd, 4096)
                except OSError:
                    return False
                if not data: return False
                out += data
        return True
    drain(delay)
    for line in lines:
        os.write(fd, line)
        if not drain(delay): break
    drain(delay)
    try:
        wpid, status = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
        if wpid == 0:
            os.kill(pid, 9)
            _, status = os.waitpid(pid, 0)
    except ChildProcessError:
        status = 0
    return out, status

if __name__ == '__main__':
    script = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    lines = [l + b'\n' for l in script.split(b'\n')[:-1]] if script else []
    out, status = run(sys.argv[1:], lines)
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(out)
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'\n[status=%d]\n' % (status >> 8))
EOF

import os, pty, sys, select, time
# sends raw bytes chunks separated by delays. chunks given as argv after '--'
def run(argv, chunks, delay=0.3):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.execvp(argv[0], argv)
    out = b''
    alive = True
    def drain(t):
        nonlocal out, alive
        end = time.time() + t
        while time.time() < end:
            r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.05)
            if r:
                try:
                    data = os.read(fd, 4096)
                except OSError:
                    alive = False
                    return
                if not data:
                    alive = False
                    return
                out += data
    drain(delay)
    for c in chunks:
        if not alive: break
        os.write(fd, c)
        drain(delay)
    drain(delay)
    try:
        wpid, status = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
        if wpid == 0:
            os.kill(pid, 9)
            _, status = os.waitpid(pid, 0)
            status = -1
    except ChildProcessError:
        status = 0
    return out, status

i = sys.argv.index('--')
argv = sys.argv[1:i]
chunks = [c.encode().decode('unicode_escape').encode('latin1') for c in sys.argv[i+1:]]
out, status = run(argv, chunks)
sys.stdout.buffer.write(out)
if status == -1:
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'\n[killed]\n')
else:
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'\n[status=%d sig=%d]\n' % (status >> 8, status & 0x7f))
EOF

impl<R: RuleType> Error<R> {
    /// Creates `Error` from `ErrorVariant` and `Position`.
    ///
    /// # Examples
    ///
    /// ```
    /// # use pest::error::{Error, ErrorVariant};
    /// # use pest::Position;
    /// # #[allow(non_camel_case_types)]
    /// # #[allow(dead_code)]
    /// # #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, Hash, Ord, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
    /// # enum Rule {
    /// #     open_paren,
    /// #     closed_paren
    /// # }
    /// # let input = "";
    /// # let pos = Position::from_start(input);
    /// let error = Error::new_from_pos(
    ///     ErrorVariant::ParsingError {
    ///         positives: vec![Rule::open_paren],
    ///         negatives: vec![Rule::closed_paren],
    ///     },
    ///     pos
    /// );
    ///
    /// println!("{}", error);
    /// ```
    pub fn new_from_pos(variant: ErrorVariant<R>, pos: Position<'_>) -> Error<R> {
        let visualize_ws = pos.match_char('\n') || pos.match_char('\r');
        let line_of = pos.line_of();
        let line = if visualize_ws {
            visualize_whitespace(line_of)
        } else {
            line_of.replace(&['\r', '\n'][..], "")
        };
        Error {
            variant,
            location: InputLocation::Pos(pos.pos()),
            line_col: LineColLocation::Pos(pos.line_col()),
            inner: Box::new(ErrorInner {
                path: None,
                line,
                continued_line: None,
                parse_attempts: None,
            }),
            ErrorVariant::ParsingError { .. } => write!(f, "parsing error: {}", self.message()),
            ErrorVariant::CustomError { .. } => write!(f, "{}", self.message()),
        }
    }
}

fn visualize_whitespace(input: &str) -> String {
    input.to_owned().replace('\r', "␍").replace('\n', "␊")
}

// Note: All builtin rules should be validated as pest builtins in meta/src/validator.rs.
// Some should also be keywords.
fn generate_builtin_rules() -> Vec<(&'static str, TokenStream)> {
    let mut builtins = Vec::new();

    insert_builtin!(builtins, ANY, state.skip(1));
    insert_builtin!(
        builtins,
        EOI,
        state.rule(Rule::EOI, |state| state.end_of_input())
    );
    insert_builtin!(builtins, SOI, state.start_of_input());
    insert_builtin!(builtins, PEEK, state.stack_peek());
    insert_builtin!(builtins, PEEK_ALL, state.stack_match_peek());
    insert_builtin!(builtins, POP, state.stack_pop());
    insert_builtin!(builtins, POP_ALL, state.stack_match_pop());
    insert_builtin!(builtins, DROP, state.stack_drop());

    insert_builtin!(builtins, ASCII_DIGIT, state.match_range('0'..'9'));
    insert_builtin!(builtins, ASCII_NONZERO_DIGIT, state.match_range('1'..'9'));
    insert_builtin!(builtins, ASCII_BIN_DIGIT, state.match_range('0'..'1'));
    insert_builtin!(builtins, ASCII_OCT_DIGIT, state.match_range('0'..'7'));
    insert_builtin!(
        builtins,
        ASCII_HEX_DIGIT,
        state
            .match_range('0'..'9')
            .or_else(|state| state.match_range('a'..'f'))
            .or_else(|state| state.match_range('A'..'F'))
    );
    insert_builtin!(builtins, ASCII_ALPHA_LOWER, state.match_range('a'..'z'));
    insert_builtin!(builtins, ASCII_ALPHA_UPPER, state.match_range('A'..'Z'));
    insert_builtin!(
        builtins,
        ASCII_ALPHA,
        state
            .match_range('a'..'z')
            .or_else(|state| state.match_range('A'..'Z'))
    );
    insert_builtin!(
        builtins,
        ASCII_ALPHANUMERIC,
        state
            .match_range('a'..'z')
            .or_else(|state| state.match_range('A'..'Z'))
            .or_else(|state| state.match_range('0'..'9'))
    );
    insert_builtin!(builtins, ASCII, state.match_range('\x00'..'\x7f'));
    insert_builtin!(
        builtins,
        NEWLINE,
        state
            .match_string("\n")
            .or_else(|state| state.match_string("\r\n"))
            .or_else(|state| state.match_string("\r"))
    );

    let box_ty = box_type();

    for property in unicode_property_names() {
        let property_ident: Ident = syn::parse_str(property).unwrap();
        // insert manually for #property substitution
        builtins.push((property, quote! {
            #[inline]
            #[allow(dead_code, non_snake_case, unused_variables)]
            fn #property_ident(state: #box_ty<::pest::ParserState<'_, Rule>>) -> ::pest::ParseResult<#box_ty<::pest::ParserState<'_, Rule>>> {
                state.match_char_by(::pest::unicode::#property_ident)
            }
        }));

//! Compiles Melody source code into an ECMAScript regular expression.

use pest::iterators::Pair;
use pest::Parser;
use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(pest_derive::Parser)]
#[grammar = "grammar.pest"]
struct MelodyParser;

/// Converts line comments (`// ...`) placed at the start of a line into block
/// comments, which is the only comment form understood by the grammar. Line
/// endings are normalised to `\n` in the process.
fn preprocess(source: &str) -> String {
    source
        .lines()
        .map(|line| match line.trim_start().strip_prefix("//") {
            Some(rest) => format!("/*{}*/", rest),
            None => line.to_string(),
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join("\n")
}

type Variables = HashMap<String, String>;

/// Compiles the given Melody source into a regular expression string.
pub fn compile(source: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let source = preprocess(source);
    let mut pairs = MelodyParser::parse(Rule::root, &source).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let root = pairs.next().expect("root rule always present");

    let mut variables = Variables::new();
    let mut output = String::new();

    for statement in root.into_inner() {
        if statement.as_rule() == Rule::EOI {
            continue;
        }
        output.push_str(&compile_statement(statement, &mut variables)?);
    }

    Ok(output)
}

fn compile_statement(pair: Pair<Rule>, variables: &mut Variables) -> Result<String, String> {
    match pair.as_rule() {
        Rule::literal => Ok(compile_literal(pair.as_str())),
        Rule::raw => Ok(compile_raw(pair.as_str())),
        Rule::range => compile_range(pair),
        Rule::symbol => compile_symbol(pair),
        Rule::negative_class => compile_negative_class(pair),
        Rule::variable_invocation => compile_variable_invocation(pair, variables),
        Rule::variable_declaration => compile_variable_declaration(pair, variables),
        Rule::quantifier => compile_quantifier(pair, variables),
        Rule::group_declaration => compile_group(pair, variables),
        Rule::assertion_declaration => compile_assertion(pair, variables),
        other => Err(format!("unexpected rule {:?}", other)),
    }
}

fn compile_block(pair: Pair<Rule>, variables: &mut Variables) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    pair.into_inner()
        .map(|statement| compile_statement(statement, variables))
        .collect()
}

];

fn escape_special(text: &str) -> String {
    let mut output = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    for character in text.chars() {
        if SPECIAL_CHARACTERS.contains(&character) {
            output.push('\\');
        }
        output.push(character);
    }
    output
}

        }
    }

    escape_special(&unescaped)

fn count_capturing_groups(chars: &[char]) -> usize {
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut in_class = false;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < chars.len() {
        match chars[i] {
            '\\' => i += 1,
            '[' => in_class = true,
            ']' => in_class = false,
            '(' if !in_class => {
                if chars.get(i + 1) != Some(&'?') {
                    count += 1;
                } else if chars.get(i + 2) == Some(&'<')
                    && !matches!(chars.get(i + 3), Some('=') | Some('!'))
                {
                    count += 1;
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    count
}

/// Collects the indices of all capture groups contained in `node`.
fn collect_captures(node: &Node) -> Vec<usize> {
    fn walk(node: &Node, out: &mut Vec<usize>) {
        match node {
            Node::Group { node, capture } => {
                if let Some(index) = capture {
                    out.push(*index);
                }
                walk(node, out);
            }
            Node::Alternation(nodes) | Node::Sequence(nodes) => {
                for inner in nodes {
                    walk(inner, out);
                }
            }
            Node::Repeat { node, .. } | Node::Look { node, .. } => walk(node, out),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    walk(node, &mut out);
    out
}

fn pattern_has_named_groups(chars: &[char]) -> bool {
    let mut i = 0;
    while i + 2 < chars.len() {
        if chars[i] == '\\' {
            i += 2;
            continue;
        }
        if chars[i] == '(' && chars[i + 1] == '?' && chars[i + 2] == '<' {
            if !matches!(chars.get(i + 3), Some('=') | Some('!')) {
                return true;
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    false
}

mod cli;
mod compiler;
mod ecma_regex;
mod repl;

use colored::Colorize;
use std::fs;
use std::io::{self, IsTerminal, Read};
use std::process;

const EXIT_USAGE: i32 = 64;
const EXIT_DATA_ERROR: i32 = 65;
const EXIT_NO_INPUT: i32 = 66;
const EXIT_IO_ERROR: i32 = 74;

fn report(message: &str) {
    eprintln!("{}", format!("Error: {}", message).bright_red());
}

fn fail(message: &str, code: i32) -> ! {
    report(message);
    process::exit(code);
}

fn read_stdin() -> Result<String, ()> {
    let mut buffer = Vec::new();
    io::stdin().read_to_end(&mut buffer).map_err(|_| ())?;
    String::from_utf8(buffer).map_err(|_| ())
}

fn no_input() -> ! {
    eprintln!(
        "{}",
        "No input file supplied and no input piped\nTry adding a path argument: 'melody ./file.mdy'"
            .bright_blue()
    );
    println!();
    let mut command = cli::command();
    let _ = command.print_help();
    process::exit(EXIT_NO_INPUT);
}

fn read_source(input: Option<&String>) -> String {
    match input.map(String::as_str) {
        Some("-") | None => {
            if io::stdin().is_terminal() {
                no_input();
            }
            match read_stdin() {
                Ok(source) => source,
                Err(()) => fail("unable to read stdin", EXIT_DATA_ERROR),
            }
        }
        Some(path) => match fs::read_to_string(path) {
            Ok(source) => source,
            Err(_) => fail(&format!("unable read file at path {}", path), EXIT_DATA_ERROR),
        },
    }
}

fn compile_regex(regex: &str) -> ecma_regex::Regex {
    match ecma_regex::Regex::new(regex) {
        Ok(compiled) => compiled,
        Err(error) => fail(
            &format!("could not compile regex\nCause: {}\nRegex: {}", error, regex),
            EXIT_DATA_ERROR,
        ),
    }
}

fn print_test_result(subject: &str, matched: bool) {
    if matched {
        println!("{} {}", subject, "matched".bright_green());
    } else {
        println!("{} {}", subject, "did not match".bright_red());
    }
}

fn main() {
    let matches = cli::command().get_matches();

    if matches.get_flag("no-color") {
        colored::control::set_override(false);
    }

    if let Some(shell) = matches.get_one::<String>("completions") {
        let stdout = io::stdout();
        let mut handle = stdout.lock();
        if !cli::write_completions(shell, &mut handle) {
            eprintln!(
                "{}",
                format!("Unknown or unsupported shell: '{}'", shell).bright_red()
            );
            eprintln!(
                "{}\n",
                "Try one of: 'bash', 'zsh', 'fish', 'elvish', 'powershell'".bright_blue()
            );
        }
        return;
    }

    if matches.get_flag("repl") {
        if !io::stdin().is_terminal() || !io::stdout().is_terminal() {
            fail("repl argument supplied with piped input or output", EXIT_USAGE);
        }
        repl::run();
        return;
    }

    let source = read_source(matches.get_one::<String>("input"));

    let regex = match compiler::compile(&source) {
        Ok(regex) => regex,
        Err(error) => fail(&error, EXIT_DATA_ERROR),
    };

    if let Some(test) = matches.get_one::<String>("test") {
        let compiled = compile_regex(&regex);
        print_test_result(&format!("'{}'", test), compiled.is_match_deep(test));
        return;
    }

    if let Some(path) = matches.get_one::<String>("test-file") {
        let compiled = compile_regex(&regex);
        let contents = match fs::read_to_string(path) {
            Ok(contents) => contents,
            Err(_) => fail(&format!("unable read file at path {}", path), EXIT_IO_ERROR),
        };
        print_test_result(path, compiled.is_match_deep(&contents));
        return;
    }

    if let Some(path) = matches.get_one::<String>("output") {
        if fs::write(path, &regex).is_err() {
            fail(path, EXIT_IO_ERROR);
        }
        return;
    }

    println!("{}", regex.bright_blue());
}

// Melody grammar (reconstructed from observed behaviour).
// NOTE: the declaration order of the rules matters, since pest sorts the
// "expected ..." lists in error messages by rule declaration order.

WHITESPACE = _{ " " | "\t" | "\n" }
COMMENT = _{ "/*" ~ (!"*/" ~ ANY)* ~ "*/" }

amount = @{ ASCII_DIGIT+ }

double_quoted_escape = _{ "\\" ~ ("\"" | "\\" | "/" | "b" | "f" | "n" | "r" | "t" | ("u" ~ ASCII_HEX_DIGIT{4})) }
single_quoted_escape = _{ "\\" ~ ("'" | "\\" | "/" | "b" | "f" | "n" | "r" | "t" | ("u" ~ ASCII_HEX_DIGIT{4})) }
literal = @{
    ("\"" ~ (double_quoted_escape | (!("\"" | "\\") ~ ANY))* ~ "\"")
  | ("'" ~ (single_quoted_escape | (!("'" | "\\") ~ ANY))* ~ "'")
}
raw = @{ "`" ~ (("\\" ~ ("`" | "\\")) | (!("`" | "\\") ~ ANY))* ~ "`" }

not = { "not" }

range = { not? ~ ((amount ~ "to" ~ amount) | (ascii_range_start ~ "to" ~ ascii_range_end)) }
quantifier_range = { amount ~ "to" ~ amount }
quantifier_quantity = { "lazy"? ~ (quantifier_range | amount | some | any | (over ~ amount) | option) ~ "of" }
group_declaration = {
    ("match" ~ block)
  | ("capture" ~ identifier? ~ block)
  | ("either" ~ block)
}
assertion_declaration = { not? ~ assertion_type ~ block }
variable_declaration = { "let" ~ "." ~ identifier ~ "=" ~ block }
variable_invocation = { "." ~ identifier }

class_content = { (ASCII_ALPHANUMERIC | "_" | " " | "!" | "#" | "$" | "%" | "&" | "*" | "@" | "\\" | "^")+ }
ascii_range_start = { ASCII }
ascii_range_end = { ASCII }
assertion_type = { "ahead" | "behind" }
some = { "some" }
any = { "any" }
option = { "option" }
over = { "over" }

block = { "{" ~ statement+ ~ "}" }
identifier = { (ASCII_ALPHA | "_")+ }
symbol_identifier = { (ASCII_ALPHA | "_")+ }

symbol = { not? ~ "<" ~ symbol_identifier ~ ">" }
negative_class = { not ~ class_content }

expression = _{ (literal | range | symbol | negative_class | raw | variable_invocation) ~ ";" }
quantifier = { quantifier_quantity ~ (expression | group_declaration | assertion_declaration | variable_declaration) }
statement = _{ expression | quantifier | group_declaration | assertion_declaration | variable_declaration }

root = { SOI ~ statement* ~ EOI }

content.text:
The work is complete. Summary of what I did:

## Approach
I reverse-engineered the `melody_cli 0.20.0` binary purely by running it (CLI flags, piped/tty stdin and stdout via Python ptys, tmux) and reading the bundled README, then wrote a from‑scratch Rust implementation.

## Implementation (`/workspace`)
- **`src/cli.rs`** – clap command definition reproducing the exact help/usage/error texts, conflicts, value names; shell completion output (zsh/fish/elvish/powershell via `clap_complete`, bash via my own generator to match the observed layout).
- **`src/grammar.pest`** – a pest grammar reconstructed by probing hundreds of malformed inputs and reasoning about pest's "expected …" attempt‑tracking rules (rule declaration order, `not?` prefixes, atomic vs. non‑atomic rules, the trailing‑whitespace span quirk) so that parse error messages are byte‑identical.
- **`src/compiler.rs`** – line‑comment preprocessing (`// …` → `/* … */` per line), compilation of literals/raw strings/symbols/ranges/negated classes/quantifiers (incl. `over N` → `{N+1,}`, group‑wrapping heuristics), groups, assertions, variables and all compile‑time error messages in the observed order.
- **`src/ecma_regex.rs`** – an ECMAScript (Annex‑B) regex parser + backtracking matcher (lookbehind, lazy quantifiers, classes, escapes incl. odd `\x` consumption, named groups) with the original engine's error strings, used for `-t` / `-f`.
- **`src/repl.rs`** – the REPL (banner, prompt, `:u/:r/:c/:s/:e`, undo/redo semantics, colouring).
- **`src/main.rs`** – I/O flow, exit codes (64/65/66/74), `colored`‑based colouring honouring `-n`, `NO_COLOR`, `CLICOLOR*`.

## Verification
Differential testing against the original: ~700 hand‑written cases plus ~10 000 fuzzed programs (grammar/error messages), ~3 000 fuzzed regex/test‑string pairs, CLI argument/pty colour matrices and fuzzed REPL sessions — all identical.

`compile.sh` builds offline with cargo (fresh clone verified) and produces `./executable`; build artifacts and the binary are git‑ignored, and all source is committed.
